We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We need to construct route using templates. We have some template IDs from search results. Need to pick plausible disconnections.

Target has: a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N- aniline). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-para-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-N-phenyl-NH2? Actually the amide is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 (para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amino group at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an amino at position 1 and another at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino at both ends? It's a phenyl with two amino groups at positions 1 and maybe 4? But the SMILES shows N attached to aromatic carbon, and the aromatic ring has another N attached at the other end (like 1,4-diaminobenzene). So the amide is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 substituent.

Thus we can think of disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline (p-tolyl amine). So we could get p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and a sulfonyl chloride derived from the other phenyl ring (4-bromophenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (4-bromophenyl sulfonyl chloride) maybe.

But we have template for sulfonamide formation: from aryl sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide. The template ID 733 from earlier: Cl-[S](=O)(=O)-c + NH2-aryl -> sulfonamide. So we can use that.

Thus step 1: target -> break sulfonamide to give aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and p-toluidine (4-methylaniline). However the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring that also has the unsaturated amide substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride would be 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring that also has the side chain (the unsaturated amide). So the sulfonyl chloride would be: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2-SO2Cl. That's a complex aryl sulfonyl chloride, maybe not commercially available. But we could consider alternative disconnection: break the C=C double bond (retro-aldol like) to give aldehyde and something? Or break amide to give acid and amine.

Better: disconnection of amide: break C(=O)-N to give carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline (the aniline with NH2). The amide is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So we could break amide to give cinnamic acid derivative (aryl acrylic acid) and aniline (p-phenylenediamine). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide is formed from a carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and p-phenylenediamine (or aniline with NH2). The acid side is the trans-α,β-unsaturated acid: (E)-4-(4-methylphenyl)sulfonyl phenyl? Wait.

The side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the acid part is (E)-4-(4-methylphenyl)sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the acid part is the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) attached to sulfonyl group and the double bond. So the acid is (E)-4-(4-methylphenyl)sulfonyl phenylacrylic acid? The double bond attaches to the phenyl ring at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has a para substituent of the unsaturated amide chain. So the acid is 4-(E)-cinnamoyl? Actually the acid is 4-(E)-cinnamoyl? The chain is phenyl-CH=CH-CO-... So the acid is 4-(E)-cinnamic acid attached to phenyl-sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl ring at the same position as the side chain? The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl ring at the same carbon as the side chain? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl ring at position 1 (the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to phenyl ring). The phenyl ring also has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 indicates the side chain is attached to the phenyl ring at position 1 (the same as the sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl via the nitrogen, not carbon. So the phenyl ring is attached to sulfonyl via N (sulfonamide). The phenyl ring also has the side chain at para position (maybe). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the phenyl ring with side chain and a sulfonyl chloride attached via S? Actually sulfonyl chloride attaches to the phenyl ring via S, not via N. So the sulfonyl chloride is Ar-SO2Cl where Ar is the phenyl ring with side chain. So that is a complex aryl sulfonyl chloride, not likely commercially available.

Alternative route: first form the amide, then sulfonamide later. So disconnection of amide first: break C=O-N to give acid (or acid chloride) and aniline (p-phenylenediamine). The acid would be (E)-4-(4-methylphenyl)sulfonyl phenylacrylic acid (Ar-CH=CH-COOH). That acid may be commercially available? Possibly not.

Alternative: break the C=C double bond (retro-aldol) to give two fragments: a phenyl aldehyde and a phenylacrylic fragment? Might be complex.

Maybe we can propose a three-step route using readily available building blocks: 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine), 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (or 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and then do Suzuki coupling to attach the side chain phenyl with unsaturated amide? Actually we could build the phenyl ring with side chain via Suzuki coupling after sulfonamide formation.

Idea: Step 1: Form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give p-tolyl-NH-SO2-4-bromophenyl. (Commercially available sulfonyl chloride). Step 2: Perform Suzuki coupling of the bromophenyl sulfonamide with a phenyl vinyl boronic acid (or a boronic acid bearing the unsaturated amide). Actually we need to attach the side chain at para position of the bromophenyl (the bromine is at para to sulfonyl). So we can do Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylic acid? Wait the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 attached to the phenyl ring at para position. So we need a phenyl ring bearing the side chain. Could be introduced via Suzuki coupling of a boronic acid that is (E)-4-(N-phenyl)acrylic acid? Actually the side chain includes a phenyl with an NH2 at para? The side chain is attached to the phenyl ring via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So the phenyl ring (the one attached to sulfonyl) is attached to the double bond at para position. So we could start from 4-bromo-phenyl-sulfonamide (product of step1) and do Heck coupling with (E)-4-aminostyrene? Actually we need to form the trans-alkene linking the phenyl ring to the carbonyl. Could use Heck reaction between aryl bromide and acrylamide (or acrylate). So step2: Heck coupling of the aryl bromide (para-bromo) with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). That would give the trans-alkene attached to carbonyl amide. Then step3: maybe protect/deprotect? But we already have amide with aniline.

Thus three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation, 2) Heck coupling, 3) maybe deprotection if needed (but none). So leaves: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, acrylamide with aniline (i.e., N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide). Is that commercially available? N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide (4-aminophenylacrylamide) maybe available. Let's check.
